newsitem.title: INDIA: India court asks state to rule on Cogentrix plant.
newsitem.headline: India court asks state to rule on Cogentrix plant.

text.p: India's Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to rule on a demand that five infrastructure projects including a large power plant by U.S.-based Cogentrix Inc be halted on environmental grounds.

The Supreme Court directed high courts in four states to rule on the plea by environmental activists, who had argued that the projects violated environmental laws. The southern state of Karnataka was asked to rule on Cogentrix's project.
"It would be better if the high courts deal with the matter as the state governments would have the opportunity to put across their point of view," the two-member Supreme Court bench said.
The judges refused to stay the projects, as demanded by petitioners Maneka Gandhi and lawyer M.C. Mehta, noted environmentalists who have opposed giant projects.
The projects include Cogentrix's 1,000-megawatt power plant at Mangalore in Karnataka, a paper and pulp project by Sinar Mas in western Maharashtra state and a cement jetty project in Gujarat.
The country's highest court said it was directing the high courts of the four states concerned to rule on the section of the petition that concerned each region.
Earlier, the government-funded National Environmental Engineering Research Institute had told the court the five infrastructure projects violated environmental regulations.

The federal government approved a counter-guarantee for the Cogentrix project in October. The counter-guarantee ensures that the power project is reimbursed in the event the state electricity board failed to pay for its power purchases.
The 1,000-megawatt power plant costing about 40 billion rupees is a joint venture between Cogentrix and a unit of China Light and Power Co Ltd.
